messages:
maria: FWIW nightly noticed a memory growth regression for long-context runs on h100/mi250x when paged KV is enabled. Token throughput drops ~25% after ~50k tokens.
zheng: Ugh. Any KV cache debug traces? sounds like fragmentation + excessive pagewalks.
devin: saw similar on a customer repro last week — eviction churn spikes then we start thrashing. Could be the page-table remap heuristic.
maria: attaching quick logs: 
```
[kv] evict_count=1423 reuse_hit=0.03 hole_count=97 pt_walks=18421 spill_bytes=3.2GiB
[perf] tokens/sec: 480 -> 360 after 55k tokens
```
zheng: hole_count 97 is suspicious. On MI250X our tiling/prefetch kernel assumes contiguous slot runs; noncontig allocation leads to extra coalescing.
sophia: @zheng do you think kernel selection fallback (to non-tiling path) would avoid the extra pagewalks?
zheng: maybe. The optimized tiled kernel uses a shadow index that breaks if pt remap inserts tombstones mid-window. Fallback would reduce throughput but stabilize memory. Worth trying.
opsbot: profiler snapshot uploaded: s3://redwood-infra/profiles/6188888888/kv-paged-6188888888.pb.gz
maria: repro steps I used (short):
```
export KV_PAGED=1
export KV_DEBUG=1
./bin/serve --model redwood/llama-paged --context 120000 --batch 1 --profile kv
```
Run on h100 w/ 80GB.
devin: also test with KV_PREFETCH_WINDOW=32 vs 64; smaller window reduced hole amplification in my runs.
sophia: can you paste a small trace of the pagewalk stack?
maria: here, trimmed: 
```
pt_walk@kv_pager.c:421 evict_idx=2048 owner=thread-7
pt_coalesce@pt_coalesce.c:87 found_hole=1 merge=0
kv_slotmap_alloc@slotmap.c:133 fallback_alloc
```
zheng: That fallback_alloc in slotmap is the culprit — it's returning segmented allocations that the tiled kernel cannot handle. I think a recent change to alloc bumping (commit b2f9c8a) relaxed contiguity checks.
devin: can we instrument a quick assert in tiled kernel that falls back if noncontig detected? Add a rare-path log so we don't slow hot path.
sophia: I can submit a small PR with guarded fallback + telemetry flag. If we flip on for nightly we can compare pt_walks and tokens/sec.
maria: To compare: nightly baseline tokens/sec 480 and pt_walks ~6k. Current failing run tokens/sec 360 and pt_walks ~18k.
opsbot: scheduled job: infra/testbench#kv-paged-longctx-6188888888 started on h100-rtxpool. Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/kv-paged-longctx/6188888888
zheng: also want to run on A100 and MI250X to confirm architecture diff. On A100 our page-alignment is fine, but MI250X prefetching threshold is different (page stripe 64 vs 128) so fragmentation shows earlier.
devin: note: NVLINK ordering can make evict completion non-deterministic across multiple GPUs leading to stale shadow entries. Could explain cross-GPU divergence in reuse hit.
sophia: proposed action items:
- add guarded tiled-kernel assert + telemetry (PR queued)
- add a perf job comparing window=32/64 and kernel fallback
- bisect commit range from b2f9c8a..HEAD to confirm change introduced contiguity relaxation
- gather KV slotmap snapshots when hole_count > 50

maria: I'll attach a small repro harness that emits `kv_slotmap_dump()` when hole_count threshold hit.
zheng: If we confirm it's alloc contiguity, fix is to adjust bump allocator to prefer coalescing holes when tiling mode active. That should keep tiled kernel fast without thrash.
devin: in parallel I'll run customer repro on A100/MI250X and paste runtime diffs.
sophia: I'm going to gate the PR behind `KV_TILE_FALLBACK=1` so we can test in staging first.
opsbot: job infra/testbench#kv-paged-longctx-6188888888 completed. Result: fail (regression reproduced). Artifacts: s3://redwood-infra/artifacts/6188888888/
maria: ok thanks. assigning: @zheng take allocator change design; @sophia PR for fallback + telemetry; @devin run cross-gpu perf matrix. I'll coordinate with QA to run the slotmap dumps.
zheng: will start on allocator patch tomorrow, will include microbench for allocation contiguity.
sophia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 includes fallback + logs.
devin: initial A100 run shows no regression; MI250X shows similar thrash as H100. So architecture-specific prefetch/stripe differences likely amplify bug.
maria: good notes. let's reconvene after allocator PR and the staged telemetry runs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
